roadmap_requirement: policy for code that remains in C indefinitely

indefinite_c_requirements.summary: The existing C implementation remains the product source of truth for the current plan horizon.

The review record must preserve the shared review-packet fields, roadmap phase, replay command, automatic return-to-blocked rule, retained closeout state, and linked scorecard/archive evidence for a stay-in-C outcome.
required_terms: parity scorecard link or blocker record

indefinite_c_requirements.summary: Only bounded surveys, manifests, validation gates, and non-goal records may continue after an explicit stay-in-C outcome.
required_terms: survey notes, boundary manifests, validation gates, and explicit non-goal records

indefinite_c_requirements.summary: There is no silent exception path; only a documented Architecture Council reopen request can reopen status review.

Every allowed exception request must stay reviewable as a bounded reopen packet with the minimum trigger, evidence, shared packet identity, automatic return-to-blocked, ownership, and source-of-truth fields kept explicit.
required_terms: decision record ID plus the current status bucket and requested decision bucket being changed
C implementation remains the product source of truth unless the reopen request is approved

indefinite_c_requirements.summary: Every active exception or reopened stay-in-C packet must fail closed with one explicit automatic return-to-blocked trigger.
required_terms: missing field, stale evidence, contradictory scorecard link, replay drift, blocker drift, or rollback-threshold breach

indefinite_c_requirements.summary: Status review may reopen only through an Architecture Council request that cites a named reopen trigger and carries the trigger-specific evidence refresh.
Each reopen trigger must point to the trigger-specific refreshed evidence by path and restate the blocker posture the new packet is trying to change.
required_terms: if multiple triggers are cited together, each trigger's minimum evidence must stay explicit

indefinite_c_requirements.summary: A retained stay-in-C packet must reuse the shared reopen-trigger catalog so later reviews do not drift in vocabulary.

The current roadmap-vs-repo survey must say plainly that the policy gap is closed locally across the dedicated note, the docs root, and the shared replay path, while leaving only the deep-core blocker posture still blocked.
required_terms: no longer a missing local governance artifact

handoff.next_step: wait for one of the named reopen triggers or the deep-core blocker posture to change before opening another Phase 15 slice

gaps.why_now: The roadmap explicitly requires a policy for code that remains in C indefinitely, and the live repo previously carried that posture only as distributed wording.
The indefinite-C policy needs a machine-checkable record so the long-term stay-in-C posture does not collapse back into prose only.
A dedicated Phase 15 test is the smallest honest way to keep the indefinite-C policy aligned with the freeze map, review process, parity scorecard, and archive templates.
The shared Phase 15 build should replay the indefinite-C policy slice alongside the rest of the governance lane.
The policy note now reuses the review-process packet fields, retained discussion state, reopen-trigger catalog, and per-anchor archive vocabulary so stay-in-C records cannot drift silently.

The parked indefinite-C policy lane now needs the same machine-checkable maintenance-mode handoff already recorded on the other Phase 15 governance surfaces so future-target wording cannot drift silently.

The dedicated indefinite-C policy packet now needs one explicit current-gap survey that keeps the local closure visible in the docs root and the shared replay path, so the remaining work stays scoped to the deep-core blocker posture rather than another missing policy artifact.
The stay-in-C exception path now needs one explicit request checklist so bounded reopen packets fail closed when trigger, evidence, identity, ownership, replay, or source-of-truth fields are missing.

The stay-in-C packet still needs one explicit automatic return-to-blocked field so active exception packets fail closed when review fields, linked evidence, scorecard state, replay commands, blocker posture, or rollback ownership drift.
The stay-in-C exception path now needs one explicit trigger-to-evidence rule so reopen requests cite the right refreshed packet evidence by path instead of relying on vague trigger names alone.

The retained stay-in-C closeout now needs one explicit landed reopen-trigger catalog entry in the same manifest so the note, manifest, focused test, and shared governance packet keep the same reopen vocabulary instead of silently drifting.
The live repo still lacks evidence strong enough to move any freeze-in-C anchor out of the current long-term C-owned posture.
